description: Verify a bounded Pocklington n-1 primality certificate with a supplied witness for each distinct prime factor of its known factored part.

source.title: The determination of the prime or composite nature of large numbers by Fermat's theorem
source.author: H. C. Pocklington
source.publisher: Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society, volume 18
source.reference: Pocklington's n-1 criterion; modern theorem statement and citation in FLINT primality-proving documentation

input.prime_factors: q_i are strictly increasing distinct primes; each exponent e_i is in 1..16
input.witnesses: 1<=a_i<n; a separate witness is supplied for every q_i

output.encoding: 1 if the supplied known-factor bound and all Pocklington witness conditions prove n prime; 0 if the frame is structurally valid but the factored part is too small or a witness condition fails; -1 for malformed framing, invalid bounds, nonprime/unsorted q_i, invalid exponent, or a factorization mismatch

contract.known_part: F=product(q_i^e_i) is fully factored by the supplied distinct prime q_i and must divide n-1 with quotient R
contract.size_condition: F^2>n is required for a proof; a structurally valid certificate with F^2<=n returns 0
contract.witness_conditions: For each distinct q_i, a_i^(n-1)=1 mod n and gcd(a_i^((n-1)/q_i)-1,n)=1; any failed congruence or gcd returns 0
contract.certificate_theorem: Acceptance proves primality by Pocklington's theorem; rejection does not assert compositeness
contract.primary_method: Trial-check each supplied q_i, accumulate F, then verify modular powers by repeated squaring and the gcd conditions by Euclid's algorithm
contract.independent_method: Trial-check q_i independently, calculate modular powers by direct repeated multiplication, and check the gcd condition by divisor enumeration
contract.distinction: This verifies a deterministic primality proof from a partial factorization of n-1; it is neither a probable-prime round test nor a general primality verdict
contract.invalid_cases: Null or non-exact framing, n outside 3..65535, k outside 1..6, unsorted/repeated/nonprime q_i, exponent outside 1..16, witness outside 1..n-1, or (F*R) != n-1 returns -1

complexity.primary_time: O(k*sqrt(n) + k*log(n)) trial division and modular arithmetic operations
complexity.independent_time: O(k*sqrt(n) + k*n) direct modular multiplications and divisor scans
